---
title: "15 — Does predictor information change in later survey years?"
output: html_notebook
---

**Research question:**
Which physical and social/demographic predictors does the frozen national model rely on in
2023, 2024, and 2025, and does their usefulness change across years?

**Measures:** survey-weighted increase in Brier error after shuffling each
predictor, using an identically frozen 2014–2022 model in each year. Also reports the
weighted FMD rate within selected predictor categories. An association or a change in
model reliance is **not** a causal relationship. The 2024 calibrator is not applied to
the importance calculations so the same base classifier is compared in all three years.
The 2025 results use the frozen model and are evaluated after model development.


```{r setup}
# Find the original RStudio project, regardless of the notebook's working directory.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(current, parent)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)

# Read the executable code blocks from existing shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(lines, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(lines) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Incomplete R code chunk in ", path)
        }
        paste(lines[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")
load_module("addon_insight_helpers")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
# Resolve the frozen model run separately from the current output run.
source_run_id <- get_source_run_id()
cat("[ADD-ON] New increment:", run_context$id, "| Original model run:", source_run_id, "\n")
```


## Load the frozen model and three annual evaluations

Each year's predictors were encoded by the original pipeline. No model fitting or
feature engineering is repeated here.

```{r load-later-years}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Original model and annual checkpoints
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Read the frozen base model and existing year-specific features from the source run.
# Keep additional outputs separate from the fitted model artifacts.

# Load the selected original model and the distinct survey-year checkpoints.
source_model <- get_source_model()
fitted <- source_model$fitted

year_2023 <- load_source_rds("checkpoints", "02_selection_2023")
year_2024 <- load_source_rds("checkpoints", "02_calibration_2024")
year_2025 <- load_source_rds("checkpoints", "07_scored_2025")

annual_data <- list(
    `2023` = year_2023,
    `2024` = year_2024,
    `2025` = year_2025
)
cat("[SOURCE MODEL]", source_model$selection$chosen_family, "\n")
```

## Compare survey-weighted predictor reliance

For speed, each year retains all available AI/AN-alone records while taking a
reproducible comparison-group sample. Inverse sampling fractions correct the weights for
the sampling stage. Independent shuffling estimates **marginal predictive reliance**,
which can be misleading for strongly correlated factors.

```{r permutation-by-year}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Annual fixed-model predictor reliance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Retain AI/AN records and subsample other cohorts with inverse-fraction weight
# adjustments.
# Compare the same uncalibrated classifier across years without refitting it.

# Choose a limited comparison sample but keep all AI/AN records in each year.
sample_for_importance <- function(data, year) {
    eligible <- data.table::copy(data.table::as.data.table(data))[
        valid_outcome(FMD) & valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT)
    ]
    set.seed(seed + as.integer(year) + 1500L)
    pieces <- lapply(unique(eligible$cohort), function(group) {
        group_data <- eligible[cohort == group]
        maximum <- if (group == primary_groups[1]) {
            nrow(group_data)
        } else if (group == primary_groups[2]) {
            35000L
        } else {
            4000L
        }
        chosen_n <- min(nrow(group_data), maximum)
        choices <- sample.int(nrow(group_data), size = chosen_n)
        sampled <- group_data[choices]
        sampled[, analysis_weight := RAW_WEIGHT * nrow(group_data) / chosen_n]
        sampled
    })
    data.table::rbindlist(pieces)
}

# Evaluate the SAME model without a new 2025-informed parameter choice.
importance_rows <- list()
model_baselines <- list()
row_id <- 0L

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (year in names(annual_data)) {
    sample_data <- sample_for_importance(annual_data[[year]], year)
    original_probabilities <- predict_classifier(fitted, sample_data)
    baseline <- weighted_metrics(
        sample_data$FMD,
        original_probabilities,
        sample_data$analysis_weight
    )
    model_baselines[[year]] <- data.frame(
        YEAR = as.integer(year),
        respondents = nrow(sample_data),
        baseline_brier = baseline$brier,
        baseline_auc = baseline$auc
    )

    for (feature in feature_names) {
        for (replicate in seq_len(if (run_mode == "quick") 3L else 7L)) {
            changed <- data.table::copy(sample_data)
            data.table::set(
                changed,
                j = feature,
                value = sample(changed[[feature]], size = nrow(changed))
            )
            new_probabilities <- predict_classifier(fitted, changed)
            new_brier <- weighted_mean(
                (changed$FMD - new_probabilities)^2,
                changed$analysis_weight
            )
            row_id <- row_id + 1L
            importance_rows[[row_id]] <- data.frame(
                YEAR = as.integer(year),
                feature = feature,
                replicate = replicate,
                baseline_brier = baseline$brier,
                permuted_brier = new_brier,
                brier_increase = new_brier - baseline$brier,
                relative_brier_increase = (new_brier - baseline$brier) / baseline$brier
            )
        }
    }
    cat("[COMPLETE]  Year:", year, "| input sample:", nrow(sample_data), "\n")
}

permutations <- data.table::rbindlist(importance_rows)
importance <- permutations[, .(
    mean_brier_increase = mean(brier_increase),
    mean_relative_increase = mean(relative_brier_increase),
    min_relative_increase = min(relative_brier_increase),
    max_relative_increase = max(relative_brier_increase)
), by = .(YEAR, feature)]


# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(data.table::rbindlist(model_baselines), "15_base_model_performance_by_year")
save_table(permutations, "15_yearly_permutation_replicates")
save_table(importance, "15_yearly_predictor_reliance")
print(importance[order(YEAR, -mean_relative_increase)])
```

## Show changing model reliance

**Measures:** the change in relative Brier deterioration when shuffling a
predictor. Differences can reflect a combination of predictive relationships,
prevalence, sample composition, and correlations between inputs.

```{r show-reliance}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Changes in relative predictor reliance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Compare relative Brier deterioration across the three survey years.
# Differences can reflect prevalence, composition, associations, and predictor
# correlations.

# The graph is printed in this notebook before being saved to the new run folder.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualization
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------


# Build the chart using the existing palette and theme; retain the original scales and
# labels.
reliance_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    importance,
    ggplot2::aes(x = YEAR, y = mean_relative_increase, color = feature)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2023:2025) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
    atg_scale_color_features() +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Frozen-model predictor reliance across later survey years",
        subtitle = "Increase in weighted Brier error after marginal permutation",
        x = "Survey year",
        y = "Relative deterioration of Brier score",
        color = "Predictor",
        caption = "2025 findings are exploratory; reliance is not a causal effect."
    )
show_and_save(reliance_plot, "15_yearly_permutation_signal", 11, 6)
```

## Examine observed FMD by predictor category

**Measures:** annual population-weighted rates of FMD within reported physical
health and household-income categories. This helps distinguish a changing predictor
distribution from a changing outcome association. Reported missing responses remain
their own category.

```{r observed-category-rates}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Observed outcomes within predictor categories
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Use all eligible primary-group records rather than the smaller importance samples.
# Calculate weighted within-category rates without adjustment for other predictors.

# Use all eligible respondents (not just the model-importance samples).
rate_rows <- list()

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (year in names(annual_data)) {
    eligible <- data.table::as.data.table(annual_data[[year]])[
        valid_outcome(FMD) & valid_weight(RAW_WEIGHT) & cohort %in% primary_groups
    ]
    for (variable in c("physical_days_group", "INCOME_BAND")) {
        grouped <- eligible[, .(
            n = .N,
            weighted_numerator = sum(FMD * RAW_WEIGHT),
            weighted_denominator = sum(RAW_WEIGHT),
            observed_fmd = weighted_mean(FMD, RAW_WEIGHT)
        ), by = .(cohort, category = as.character(get(variable)))]
        grouped[, `:=`(YEAR = as.integer(year), feature = variable)]
        rate_rows[[length(rate_rows) + 1L]] <- grouped
    }
}
category_rates <- data.table::rbindlist(rate_rows)

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(category_rates, "15_yearly_fmd_by_predictor_category")
print(category_rates[order(feature, cohort, YEAR, category)])

# Two facets keep both predictor-category rates legible within the notebook.

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (variable in c("physical_days_group", "INCOME_BAND")) {
    chart_data <- category_rates[feature == variable]
    category_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
        chart_data,
        ggplot2::aes(x = factor(YEAR), y = observed_fmd, fill = category)
    ) +
        ggplot2::geom_col(position = "dodge") +
        ggplot2::facet_wrap(~cohort) +
        ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
        atg_scale_fill_categories(chart_data$category) +
        atg_theme() +
        ggplot2::labs(
            title = paste("Observed FMD by", variable, "category"),
            subtitle = "Survey-weighted within-category rates; no adjustment for other factors",
            x = "Survey year",
            y = "Observed frequent mental distress",
            fill = "Category",
            caption = "Small category sample sizes can produce unstable observed rates."
        )
    show_and_save(category_plot, paste0("15_outcome_by_", variable), 11, 6)
}
```
